policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV's 'at the two ends was it joined together' permits both the qere קְצוֹתָיו and the ketiv קצוותו as plural expressions for its ends; no mapped textual note distinguishes them, so the base qere remains the fallback.
ASV explicitly renders the plural 'its bars,' distinguishing the qere בְּרִיחָיו from the singular ketiv בריחו.
